input.title: Use the report's local date, not UTC, in export file names
input.body:
File: src/exportUtils.ts

formatExportFilename builds the date suffix with `at.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, which is always the UTC calendar date. For a user west of UTC, an evening export's local date is one day behind UTC, so the file name lands on tomorrow's date. The filename should be built from the exporting user's (or account's) local time zone, similar to how src/util/dates.ts already formats dates for a given tz, instead of always using UTC.

input.title: Keep the "(copy)" suffix visible when duplicating a long report name
input.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

The duplicate endpoint builds the copy's name as `truncate(`${source.name} (copy)`, MAX_NAME_LENGTH)`. When source.name is already near the 120-character limit, truncate() cuts the combined string and appends "...", which drops the " (copy)" suffix entirely and leaves the copy's visible name identical to the original's. The name should instead be built by truncating source.name to leave room for the " (copy)" suffix (e.g. truncate(source.name, MAX_NAME_LENGTH - " (copy)".length) + " (copy)"), so the suffix always survives.

input.title: Preserve non-Latin letters in export file names instead of dropping them
input.body:
File: src/util/strings.ts

slugify() normalizes with NFKD, strips combining marks, and then replaces anything outside [a-z0-9] with a hyphen, which removes Greek, Cyrillic and other non-Latin scripts entirely (while accented Latin letters survive via decomposition). formatExportFilename falls back to "report" whenever slugify returns an empty string, which is why non-Latin report names all export as "report-<date>". slugify should keep letters from other scripts (e.g. widen the allowed character class instead of restricting to a-z0-9) so these names stay distinguishable in exported file names.

input.title: Clear the previous upload error when a new file is chosen
input.body:
File: src/components/UploadForm.tsx

The file input's onChange handler only calls setFile and never clears the `problem` state set by a previous failed upload, so the old error (and row number) stays visible under the form after a new file is picked, until the next submit. The onChange handler should also call setProblem(null) when a new file is selected.

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/exportUtils.ts

formatExportFilename() takes the date suffix from `at.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, which is the UTC calendar date, not the exporter's local date. Anyone west of UTC who exports in the evening gets a file dated tomorrow (in UTC) because the local day hasn't rolled over yet. The fix should build the date from the exporting user's/account's local time zone (per the discussion: "the day we export, in our own time zone"), not UTC. Opened a draft PR with the proposed direction.

label: question
file: none

Yes: src/util/money.ts stores and operates on amounts as integer "minor units" (e.g. cents), never as floating point decimals. parseAmount() converts the text in an uploaded file into an integer by rounding `Number(text) * 10 ** minorDigits(currency)`, and all arithmetic in exports/totals stays on that integer until formatMinor/formatMoney convert it back to a display string. Zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW, CLP, ISK, VND, XAF, XOF) are handled via a dedicated list in minorDigits(), so they're treated as having 0 minor digits instead of the default 2, avoiding the "100 yen stored as 1.00" mistake. No code change is needed for this.

label: bug
file: src/api/reports.ts

The duplicate endpoint builds the new name as `truncate(`${source.name} (copy)`, MAX_NAME_LENGTH)`. truncate() cuts the whole combined string and appends "..." once it exceeds the limit, so when source.name is already close to 120 characters, the " (copy)" suffix gets cut off entirely and the result is indistinguishable from the original in the list. The name should be built by reserving room for " (copy)" first (truncating source.name to MAX_NAME_LENGTH - " (copy)".length before appending), so the suffix is always present. Opened a draft PR with this fix.

label: feature
file: src/util/strings.ts

slugify() runs an NFKD normalize, strips combining marks (which is what lets accented Latin letters like "é" degrade gracefully to "e"), then replaces anything outside [a-z0-9] with a hyphen. Greek and Cyrillic letters have no Latin decomposition, so they're removed outright, and formatExportFilename() falls back to the literal string "report" whenever slugify() returns empty — which is why every export from a non-Latin-named report is named "report-<date>". Widening the allowed character class in slugify() to keep letters from other scripts (rather than restricting to ASCII) would let these file names stay distinct. Opened a draft PR for this.

label: bug
file: src/components/UploadForm.tsx

The file input's onChange only calls setFile(e.target.files?.[0] ?? null); it never clears the `problem` state that a previous failed upload set, so the old error and row number stay rendered under the form until the user submits again. The onChange handler should also call setProblem(null) whenever a new file is chosen. Opened a draft PR with this fix.

text:
All five issues have been triaged:

1. **issue-4424** — `bug` — `src/exportUtils.ts`: export filenames use UTC date instead of the exporter's local date (PR pr-25).
2. **issue-4426** — `question` — no file: confirmed amounts are stored as integer minor units in `src/util/money.ts`, with zero-decimal currencies handled explicitly; nothing to change.
3. **issue-4429** — `bug` — `src/api/reports.ts`: duplicate's "(copy)" suffix gets truncated away for long names (PR pr-26).
4. **issue-4431** — `feature` — `src/util/strings.ts`: `slugify()` strips non-Latin scripts entirely, causing all non-Latin report names to export as "report-<date>" (PR pr-27).
5. **issue-4434** — `bug` — `src/components/UploadForm.tsx`: stale upload error isn't cleared when a new file is chosen (PR pr-28).
